audit.summary: Admissible radial solution disproves the forcing identity in the nonzero-flux application proof. Local correction preserves the decay estimates. Core full-space rigidity argument remains supported in inspected scope.
limitations: Limitations: Only arXiv2306.05184v2 of2 September2023 is assessed; publisher abstract differs and byte equivalence is not established.
Limitations: All26 extracted text pages actually read; external Stokes regularity, Bogovskii estimates and cited removable-singularity criterion were not independently reproved.
Limitations: No counterexample to the principal rigidity, removal, or decay conclusions is asserted.
Limitations: Actual source and report image viewing is blocked by EMFILE.
Counterevidence: Read the smallness quantifier, zero-flux reduction and the subsequent convolution/uniqueness bounds; the repair does not require an unverified numerical lower bound on epsilon.
Counterevidence: The source's no-slip part is dimension four only. No nonzero globally C/r-bounded solution is inferred from the local diagnostic.
Limits: Cited local Stokes estimates treated as inputs.
Limits: External Bogovskii and regularity results not reproved; weighted functional-space completion is made explicit in report.
The finding applies to the exact reviewed source version and inspected scope; uninspected publication versions are not adjudicated.
The report retains counterevidence and unresolved questions. Publication does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific adjudication remains pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim:
For u1=u-a, a=cx/|x|^n and p_a=-|a|^2/2, the extended u1 satisfies equation(73) with the displayed forcing.

With the printed h=-integral(partial_r u dot u-|u|^2 u^r/2-pu^r), the annular Dirichlet energy is h(R2)-h(R1).

repair.content:
